market: DET −6.5, total 49.5. Goff 31.5 attempts / 21.5 completions; Willis 27.5 / 17.5 and 5.5 rushes. Gibbs 20.5 carries; Ollie Gordon II 16.5.
lineup: DET's defense is missing CB D.J. Reed, S Kerby Joseph and LBs Jack Campbell and DJ Wonnum. Amon-Ra St. Brown is questionable (ribs), C Cade Mays is out, Isiah Pacheco is out and Sione Vaki is questionable. MIA RBs Kaytron Allen and Jaylen Wright are questionable.
branches: If Amon-Ra sits, Jameson Williams and LaPorta absorb his 31% share. If both Allen and Wright sit, Gordon's share of MIA carries rises from about 52%.

keys.take: MIA's ground game. MIA ran 39 times in its one-score win over the Jets.
keys.how: Build a lead. Opponents run only 22.4 times a game against DET because they're usually chasing.
keys.gives: The middle of the field. With Joseph and Campbell out, DET allows 97.7 TE yards a game (worst here) and 4.7 completions of 20+ yards a game.
keys.counter: Willis to the TE and Willis scrambles. He's had five or more scrambles in four games.

keys.take: Gibbs, who gets 78% of DET's carries and averages 110 rushing yards.
keys.how: MIA's run defense is decent (4.18 yards per carry), but it gets worn down. Opponents run 27.7 times a game.
keys.counter: DET's control script. Gibbs averaged 25 carries in DET's five wins.

scripts.control: DET leads (about a 75% favorite). MIA throws, as it did averaging 28.7 attempts in losses of 8+. Gordon's carries fall: 17 for 41 yards in the 24–10 loss to KC. Dulcich and Washington get the volume.
scripts.competitive: MIA runs Gordon 20+ times and keeps the ball. This is the script that beats the Gordon under.
scripts.reversal: MIA leads on Willis's legs. Gibbs' carries drop to his loss-game level (15–16 carries, 46–52 yards).

plays.line: Ollie Gordon II under 70 rushing yards (No)
plays.why: DET is a 6.5-point favorite, and teams facing DET run the fewest times in the league because they're behind. Gordon's yards depend on MIA leading.
plays.support: Opponents average 22.4 rushes a game against DET (fewest here). Our backtest: rushing-yard Yes prices have come in about 8 points below price.
plays.sample: Gordon cleared 70 in 3 of 6, and all 3 came with MIA within one score. In MIA's lone loss of 8+ with him as the lead back, he ran for 41.
plays.counter: Allen and Wright questionable could push his carries past 20. He ran 9 times for 100 at MIN.
plays.loses: MIA keeps it within a score into the fourth and leans on him (25 carries for 103 against the Jets).
plays.vs: Beat the 75-yard No (57¢, needs 59%): extra cost for a 5-yard cushion.

plays.why: The trailing script plus DET's missing middle defenders (Joseph, Campbell) points targets at MIA's TE.
plays.support: DET allows 11.4 TE targets and 97.7 TE yards a game. TEs caught 4+ against them in 5 of 7 games (Kincaid 7, Sadiq 7, McBride 9, Kraft 4, Hockenson 4).
plays.sample: Dulcich caught 4+ in each of the last 4 (5, 4, 5, 4) on a 19–24% target share. Overall 4 of 6.
plays.counter: MIA throws only 26 times a game, and Washington (25% share) is the first read.
plays.loses: MIA keeps it close and runs 35 times, so Willis throws 20 passes.
plays.vs: Preferred over 40+ yards (51¢). Receptions fit the short-middle thesis, and our backtest marks receiving-yard Yes prices as rich.

passed.name: Jahmyr Gibbs 100+ rush (50¢)
passed.why: The control script helps (4 of 5 wins over 100), but MIA has held lead backs under 100 in 5 of 7, and our backtest leans against rushing Yes prices. The two cancel.
passed.move: Vaki inactive plus a price under 46¢.

passed.name: Malik Willis 30+ rush (51¢), either side
passed.why: His results split into two clusters (39–74 yards or 2–11) with nothing in between. We can't estimate a probability for that.

passed.name: Amon-Ra St. Brown props
passed.why: Questionable (ribs), and MIA allows the fewest WR targets of any defense here (12.4 a game).
passed.move: Active and no snap limit reported.
